subject.title: feat: Force reply to originating channel (Telegram/Discord/WhatsApp)

question: Should OpenClaw make external-origin reply delivery a durable automatic invariant, add an explicit opt-in force/fallback policy, or keep the current WebChat and same-surface gates with narrower channel-specific fixes?
rationale: The next change can alter which external conversation receives generated content, so code inspection cannot decide the product and privacy boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt durable turn-origin delivery
options.body: Capture the inbound turn's external channel, account, target, and thread once, preserve it through the agent and follow-up pipeline, and route final replies there unless the turn explicitly chooses another route.

options.title: Add opt-in force/fallback policy
options.body: Keep current defaults but add a documented default-off policy for force-origin or fallback delivery with schema, doctor/docs, authorization, route freshness, and live-channel proof.

options.title: Keep gates and fix narrow bugs
options.body: Leave WebChat and same-surface suppression as the security default and address only proven channel-specific delivery defects such as WhatsApp same-surface drops.

recommendation.title: Adopt durable turn-origin delivery
recommendation.body: Capture the inbound turn's external channel, account, target, and thread once, preserve it through the agent and follow-up pipeline, and route final replies there unless the turn explicitly chooses another route.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current routing-gate provenance and recent area history across the central reply-routing files.
